openings.claim: Switching may disrupt selection/checking or placement/insertion sequence.
openings.discriminator: Staging reduces selection/checking time and discrepancies; sequence cues reduce transition-specific insertion corrections.
openings.probe: Reuse 12 samples; counterbalance both workers and comparable layouts across current/staged selection, repeated/alternating layouts and cue/no cue. Log each work stage, discrepancies, corrections and retries.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity confounds switching; bench space and delivery slack remain unverified.

openings.claim: Generic diagrams may obscure the short partition’s ordered position despite correct contents.
openings.discriminator: Order-specific diagrams improve unaided success and reduce questions with identical verified contents.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten participants to current/order-specific diagrams; record first-exposure success, questions and insertion failures.
openings.uncertainty: Small comparison is directional; complaints do not establish verified packing errors.

openings.claim: Slot condition or alignment may create difficult pairings despite overlapping widths.
openings.discriminator: Retries persist at particular slots/pairings despite cues and regardless of preceding layout.
openings.probe: Reuse samples; exchange matched-width parts among compatible slots with controlled insertion order. Record pairing, edge condition and attempts; counterbalance repetitions for wear.
openings.uncertainty: Widths do not establish cause; transition-following failures favor D1 sequence interference.

lineage.reason: Selection/checking mechanism preserved separately from insertion sequencing.
Sequence interference and cue discriminator preserved.

decision: Probe before adoption; synthetic observations establish no pilot success. Preserve 30×20 cm footprint, capacity, removable joints, accepted counts/colors and fixed delivery; require ≤500 initial and ≤0.40/order. Retain packaging provisionally. Full assembly’s completeness and starting-arrangement benefits remain hypotheses.
